outcome_detail: Both halves the gap names now exist together: a real project workflow (not the synthetic planner fixture) recovered across an orderly restart, and the unchanged upstream Dagu retry tests at v2.16.6 ran in the same invocation with both oracles in one result. Remaining: the restart is a user+pid+mount-namespace analog, not the disposable Ubuntu guest kernel reboot with a lingering systemd user timer that the service-reboot protocol specifies. Binding blocker: the protocol driver refuses to run anywhere except the declared disposable GitHub-hosted runner (blueprints/convergence-practice/service-reboot/run.py lines 149-150: `if os.environ.get('GITHUB_ACTIONS') != 'true' or os.environ.get('RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT') != 'github-hosted': raise ValueError('Execution requires the declared disposable GitHub-hosted runner')`), and dispatching the hosted workflow would need a pushed branch, which this unit may not create. Why a local port of the protocol was not attempted (not a hard blocker): qemu-system-x86_64, qemu-img and cloud-localds are absent, and this user is not in the kvm group (/dev/kvm is root:kvm 0660). Rootless options exist and were not tried: fetch the packages with `apt-get download` and unpack them with `dpkg -x` into the cache, then boot the guest under QEMU TCG without /dev/kvm. Such a port would also have to change or bypass the driver's guard, so it would no longer be the unchanged protocol. (Fix round 3 corrected an earlier wording that called the qemu packages and the kvm group blockers needing sudo.)
